definitions.gloss: opening; the first part of something
definitions.explanation: The very beginning of a piece of writing, a speech, a song, or a race — the part that sets the tone for what follows. It is nearly always used with an evaluation attached: a good {出|で}だし or a bad one.

examples.english: It's off to a good start.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{出|で}だしが{印象的|いんしょうてき}だ。
examples.english: This novel has a striking opening.

examples.japanese: {出|で}だしでつまずいたが、{後半|こうはん}で{順位|じゅんい}を{取|と}り{戻|もど}した。
examples.english: He stumbled at the start, but got his position back in the second half.

notes:
The noun form of {出|で}る (to come out) plus だし, literally "the coming-out part."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出|で}だしが{好調|こうちょう}だ: to get off to a strong start
- {出|で}だしでつまずく: to stumble at the start
- {出|で}だしの{一行|いちぎょう}: the opening line
- {出|で}だしから{飛|と}ばす: to go all out from the start

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {冒頭|ぼうとう}: the opening — more formal, and used mainly of texts, speeches, and meetings
- スタート: start — the moment of setting off, rather than the opening stretch
- {書|か}き{出|だ}し: opening lines — specifically the first words of a piece of writing
